claim: A voltage divider scales a battery voltage down into an ADC's range: Vout = Vin × R2 ÷ (R1 + R2).
draft: The M5StickC Plus2 (ESP32-PICO) already has a 2:1 divider on GPIO38 for its own battery, so the 2S pack needs a separate ADC1 pin: G32 or G33 on the Grove port. ADC2 pins (e.g. G26) don't work while WiFi or ESP-NOW runs. For 8.4 V full charge: 3:1 protects the pin but lands at 2.8 V, in the non-linear zone; about 4:1 (300k/100k) lands at 2.1 V. 300k + 100k draws about 21 µA, so add 100 nF at the pin.

claim: A voltage divider scales a battery voltage down into an ADC's range: Vout = Vin × R2 ÷ (R1 + R2).
draft: Size it so a full pack reads inside the ADC's accurate range, not just its safe range. On a classic ESP32 that means under about 2.45 V at 11 dB attenuation. Above that, readings bend even with calibration.

claim: A logic-level N-channel MOSFET can switch a load from a 3.3 V GPIO if it's specified to switch fully on at that gate voltage.
draft: The AO3400 (SOT-23) is rated with Rds(on) at Vgs = 2.5 V, so it suits a 3.3 V GPIO. The IRLZ44N is only rated at 4–5 V and is marginal from 3.3 V, especially above an amp. Check every part against your load current.

claim: The SCP substrate logs every write to an append-only events table, with archiving as the one exception.
draft: The move itself is already logged: archive.moved records the archive file and the counts of what left. What's still missing is proof. Add the archive file's sha256 to that event, and the moved history can be checked against it.

claim: The assembled ACEBOTT spider chassis spans about 159 mm per side.
draft: Source: the listing's dimension image. It conflicts with the item details; see spider-chassis-listing-dimensions-conflict. Span changes with leg pose, so record the pose you measure at.

claim: The assembled ACEBOTT spider chassis stands about 82 mm tall.
draft: Source: the listing's dimension image. It conflicts with the item details; see spider-chassis-listing-dimensions-conflict.

claim: The ACEBOTT spider chassis body is made of acrylic plates.
draft: Sources: Ernestina's Vine review (11-03-2025) and the listing image labelled 'Acrylic Board'. Acrylic is light and stiff but brittle at holes and edges, so snug the screws, don't crank them, and avoid thread-locker that attacks acrylic.

claim: On the ACEBOTT spider, the battery has to go in during assembly, not after.
draft: Source: Ernestina's Vine review of the stock kit. The stock bay takes one 18650 flat-top cell; see spider-chassis-one-18650-flat-top and scpbot-chassis-modded-for-7-4v-packs.

claim: On the ACEBOTT spider, the battery has to go in during assembly, not after.
draft: It's one reviewer on the stock chassis. SCPBot's bay is modified for two 2S packs, so the order may not apply. Fitting the cell early also means the frame is live while you're screwing it together.

claim: The ACEBOTT spider chassis is held together with M3 x 25 mm dual-pass copper pillars.
draft: Source: the listing image 'Powerful Hardware'. 'Dual-pass' means female threads at both ends. Most cheap 'copper' pillars are brass; it doesn't matter structurally.

claim: The ACEBOTT spider chassis has four legs.
draft: Source: the listing copy and images ('four-legged'). The review that says '8 legs' is most likely counting the 8 servos.

claim: The ACEBOTT listing gives two sizes that disagree: 82 mm tall and 159 mm wide in its image, but 5.1 x 10.2 x 12.7 cm in its item details.
draft: Sources: the listing's dimension image against its item details. 5.1 × 10.2 × 12.7 cm is exactly 2 × 4 × 5 inches, which smells like a packaging size.

claim: The ACEBOTT spider chassis holds one 18650 flat-top cell, and button-top cells don't fit.
draft: Sources: the listing copy and image, plus Ernestina's review. A flat-top 18650 is about 65 mm long and a button-top about 67–69 mm, which is why button-tops won't fit. This describes the stock chassis; SCPBot's bay is modified.

claim: The ACEBOTT spider chassis parts fit together without modification.
draft: Sources conflict: Ernestina's Vine review says everything fitted, and another review reports wrong parts in the box. Kit quality varies by batch, so your own unit is the only evidence that counts for SCPBot.

claim: The ACEBOTT spider's stock feet can fail to grip a laminate floor.
draft: Source: Ry01's review (07-09-2026). The paired fix is in spider-chassis-rubber-feet-fix.

claim: The ACEBOTT spider's stock feet can fail to grip a laminate floor.
draft: It's one review on one floor. Grip depends on the floor, the robot's weight and the gait; SCPBot is heavier with two packs, which may actually help grip while costing torque.

claim: Assembling the ACEBOTT spider chassis is repetitive, because every leg is built the same way.
draft: Source: Ernestina's Vine review. Four identical legs with two servos each means the horn angle and servo centring must match on all four before the gait code can be symmetrical. Centre each servo (90°) before fitting its horn.

claim: Adding non-slip rubber to the ACEBOTT spider's feet improves its grip.
draft: Source: Ry01's review (07-09-2026), one owner's fix. Their 'no faster than a slug' suggests the real limit is MG90S torque under load or the stock gait, not just grip.

claim: Assembling the ACEBOTT spider chassis means positioning very small nuts, which is fiddly.
draft: Source: Ernestina's Vine review. The nuts are probably M2 or M3 going into acrylic pockets; a magnetised driver, or a dab of Blu Tack in the pocket, holds them while the screw starts.

claim: Assembling the ACEBOTT spider chassis means positioning very small nuts, which is fiddly.
draft: It's one reviewer's experience, and fiddly isn't a fault. It just costs time and dropped nuts.

claim: Each ACEBOTT spider leg has two servo-driven joints, eight servos in total.
draft: Inferred from listing images. Two joints per leg (hip and knee) times four legs gives 8 servos, which fills 8 of the PCA9685's 16 channels.

claim: Each ACEBOTT spider leg has two servo-driven joints, eight servos in total.
draft: The listing never states it. It's inferred from images, and an image can hide a third joint or show a different kit revision.

claim: The ACEBOTT spider chassis uses the same screws throughout.
draft: Source: the seller's listing copy. Seller claims are marketing until checked; a quick sort of the hardware bag by length settles it.
